answer: Admission treats each identity as a distinct vine cultivar releasing its pollen plume only inside a sealed flowering window. A laboratory sequences a sable marker panel whose length equals the current seat count plus one and rejects any haplotype shared with a seated cultivar. The m-th entrant therefore faces m(m-1) independent comparisons, and k entrants require k(k+1)(k-1)/3 in total. Each candidate supplies its own living tissue, so one sample cannot certify several identities.
